h1: At the till, once a customer has bought cheese on a dairy-sale day, regular-price orders rung up afterwards come out cheaper than the shelf price for the rest of the session; restarting the till fixes it. Example: a regular order of 1 cheese plus 1 milk rang up 1558 cents when the shelf prices add to 1688.
h2: On the live dashboard the West whole-dollar tile, ReportConfig('west', rounding=0), shows 185.68 instead of 186.0. A colleague who ran the same thing locally says it showed 186.0 for her.
h3: Finance's month-end reconciliation says acct-20 should close at -3606.00, but ledger.book.balances() gives -3894.06, which is 288.06 away. acct-13 and the other accounts reconcile.
h4: The invoice for order 1042 comes out short: the customer was billed for the milk and the rice but not for the cheese. The other orders in data/orders.json invoice correctly, and the price list has cheese at 12.99.
h5: About one in ten order totals from billing.orders.order_total is one cent below what accounting's system computes for the same order, always low, and nothing else about those orders looks unusual. Example: order o007.
h6: The standings printed by `python -m board.cli entries.json` list tied players in a different order from one run to the next, with the same file and no code changes, so ranks swap between deploys.
h7: Since the US clocks changed on 8 March, the daily 'digest' job for America/New_York (first run 2026-03-06 06:00 local) fires at 07:00 local every day instead of 06:00. Our tests run in UTC and never noticed.
h8: Requests for tenant 'acme' sometimes go out with another tenant's X-Tenant header, and an anonymous client occasionally sends a tenant header at all. It only started once the batch job began building many clients in one process; a single client on its own looks fine.
h9: CSV exports started from the dashboard's 'preview, then download' flow, export_csv(preview=True), come out with rows missing. The plain download, export_csv(), is complete.
h10: On the new build server the service starts with max_workers=4 and log level 'info'; on everyone's laptop it comes up with 16 workers and 'warning' from the same checkout and the same conf.d files.
L1: `python -m freightdesk quote --carrier NORDLINE --to DE-80331 --parcel 45x35x18@2 --ship-date 2026-10-05` quotes EUR 9.11 (billable 5 kg), but by Nordline's current rate card that parcel bills at 6 kg and should cost EUR 12.15. A handful of other parcels in our October manifest are also undercharged, while most quotes come out right.
L2: For our full-year export, `python -m ledgerly invoice total data/invoices_2025.csv` prints a grand total of 4,280,950.84 USD (which matches the billing system), but `python -m ledgerly report summary data/invoices_2025.csv --payments data/payments_2025.json` prints 4,280,950.30 USD for the same file, and its Collected figure (3,459,491.20 USD) is also off (we expect 3,459,491.79 USD). On the small Q3 sample file both commands agree.
L3: When we load the monthly exports with `python -m stockflow batch data/movements --workers 8`, the totals occasionally come out wrong: every so often the report's MOVEMENTS and TOTAL ON HAND are way off what `python -m stockflow import data/movements/*.csv` reports for the same files (1,472 movements, 11,085 on hand), even though the progress lines show every file fully posted. Rerunning the same batch command usually gives the right numbers again, and `import` has never been wrong.
L4: On the Mumbai office's reporting server, `python -m tillbook daily-totals --office BOM --date 2026-03-14` reports 22 sales and a net of 58,102.00 INR, but the tills recorded 24 sales and a net of 62,842.00 INR for that Mumbai day (the same command on our UTC box in London gives the right numbers). The difference is made up of online orders and refunds from late in the evening, around midnight.
L5: Customer order SO-1042 has all 10 units of LMP-220 on backorder at MAIN. After we received two partial deliveries (`python -m stockroom receive LMP-220 4 --warehouse MAIN`, then `... receive LMP-220 6 --warehouse MAIN`), `python -m stockroom report availability --sku LMP-220` shows MAIN with 10 on hand, only 4 reserved and 6 available, so the system let another customer order lamps that are already promised to SO-1042; we expected 10 reserved and 0 available.
L6: We raised batch_size under [delivery] in config/relaydesk.toml to 50, but `python -m relaydesk send --dry-run` still splits every channel into batches of at most 20 (support goes out as 20, 20, 20, 20, 2). Changing that value to anything else makes no difference either, while other settings in the same file (endpoint, retry attempts) are picked up fine.
L7: Running `python -m ledgerkit export data/sample.ledger -o report.csv` gives a normal comma-separated file on my laptop, but on our CI runner the exact same command and checkout writes semicolon-separated values with dates like 02.01.2026 and amounts like 4250,00. Passing `-f csv` explicitly works everywhere.
L8: Since the last release the nightly import (`python -m stockline import --full-feed acme_2026-10-28.csv`, about 200k rows) takes around 40 minutes instead of a few seconds. The small sample feeds in samples/ still finish instantly, and the imported data looks correct; it is only slow, and it gets much slower the bigger the feed is.
L9: Running `python -m basketry summarize samples/requests.jsonl`, Grace Hopper's receipt for order W-1002 (two mugs and a honey) lists "Gift wrap: Merino Wool Scarf" and "Gift message card: "Happy birthday, Mum!"" under "Packed with your order", which belong to Ada Lovelace's order W-1001 earlier in the batch. Summarizing W-1002 on its own gives a correct receipt; other receipts later in the batch pick up items from earlier customers too.
L10: Running `python -m ledgerflow import config/partner.toml --validate` reports "acme-feed: 86 imported, 0 rejected, 0 duplicates", but the ACME feed has 120 transactions since 2026-09-01 and without --validate all 120 are imported; the missing ones are the earliest September transactions. Our nightly job (no --validate) also comes up short, with the earliest transactions absent, on nights when the log shows "acme-feed: attempt 1 failed ... retrying".
